target.title: fix(google): anchor model-ID regexes to prevent false-positive substring matches
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Model-ID matching in `google-shared.ts` uses unanchored substring patterns:
- `model.id.includes("2.5-pro")` matches `gemini-2.5-pro-exp` and `not-gemini-2.5-pro`
- `/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro/` matches `not-gemini-3-pro-vision`
- `/gemma-?4/` matches `not-gemma-4-pro`

These false-positives can silently route the wrong thinking budget/config to a different model variant.

**Solution**: Anchor all model-ID regexes with `(?:^|\/)` prefix and `\b` word boundary suffix. Also replace `String.includes()` calls with properly anchored regex tests.

**Per ClawSweeper review**: The MIME type validation (previously in this PR) has been **removed**. Only the regex anchoring fixes remain.

## Real behavior proof

```
$ npx tsx _validate-regex-anchors.mts
=== Model-ID regex anchoring proof ===

  ✓ gemma-4: "models/gemma-4" → true (valid match)
  ✓ gemma-4 substring: "not-gemma-4-pro" → false (OLD false positive, NEW rejected)
  ✓ gemini-3-pro: "models/gemini-3-pro" → true (valid match)
  ✓ gemini-3-pro substring: "not-gemini-3-pro-vision" → false (OLD false positive, NEW rejected)
  ✓ gemini-3-flash: "models/gemini-3-flash" → true (valid match)
  ✓ gemini-3-flash substring: "not-gemini-3-flash-lite" → false (OLD false positive, NEW rejected)
  ✓ gemini-2.5-pro valid: "models/gemini-2.5-pro" → true
  ✓ gemini-2.5-pro substring: "not-gemini-2.5-pro-exp" → false
  ✓ gemini-2.5-flash-lite: "models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite" → true
  ✓ gemini-2.5-flash-lite substring: "not-gemini-2.5-flash-lite-x" → false
  ✓ gemini-2.5-flash: "models/gemini-2.5-flash" → true
  ✓ gemini-2.5-flash vs flash-lite: "models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite" → false (NOT matched as flash)

✅ 12 passed, 0 failed
```

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` → exit 0 ✓
- Existing google-shared test suite passes (including updated regex tests)

/cc @openclaw/clawsweeper
